summary.title: Building a neural network from scratch in Go
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a single-hidden-layer neural network in Go using only gonum matrices and no cgo, trained with backpropagation on a noisy iris dataset to about 97% accuracy.
keywords: how to train neural net in go
takeaways: A neural net's nodes combine inputs linearly with weights and biases, then apply a non-linear activation such as sigmoid.
Backpropagation loop: randomly initialize weights and biases, feed forward, compare to labels, compute gradients, and update parameters over many epochs.
Helper functions like sumAlongAxis and gonum matrix operations handle the bias gradients and layer math without cgo.
The network is trained on a slightly transformed iris dataset with one-hot species labels and added noise, reaching about 0.97 accuracy on the test split.
summary.summary: The author walks through building a small neural network in Go with no cgo, using gonum matrices so inputs can be supplied like numpy arrays and node counts can be configured. The article defines the network structure, a sigmoid activation and its derivative, a train method that runs backpropagation with stochastic gradient descent for a set number of epochs, and a predict method that performs feed-forward. It then trains on a noisy, one-hot encoded iris dataset (80/20 train/test split) and measures subset accuracy, which comes out around 97% in the example run. Full code and data are linked on GitHub.
